findings.explanation: HOL4 introduces `instance` by new_specification. The only saved theorem, instance_def, fixes `instance tmsig i name ty` when FLOOKUP tmsig name = SOME ty0 and ty = TYPE_SUBST tyin ty0. It says nothing when the name is undeclared or ty is not an instance of the declared type. Lean's definition has an else branch, so Lean proves `instance_ tmsig i name ty = fun _ => tmaof i name []` on exactly those inputs, for example tmsig = FEMPTY. Through termsem, Lean then also proves termsem of any undeclared constant equals tmaof i name []. HOL4 leaves these equations open.
findings.repair:
def instance_ [Inhabited U] : tmsig → interpretation U → mlstring → type → tyval U → U :=
  ε (fun f : tmsig → interpretation U → mlstring → type → tyval U → U =>
    ∀ (tmsig : tmsig) (i : interpretation U) (name : mlstring) (ty ty0 : type) (tyin : List (type × type)),
      FLOOKUP tmsig name = some ty0 ∧ ty = TYPE_SUBST tyin ty0 →
      f tmsig i name ty = fun τ => tmaof i name
        (MAP (typesem (tyaof i) τ ∘ TYPE_SUBST tyin ∘ Tyvar)
          (MAP .implode (STRING_SORT (MAP explode (tyvars ty0))))))
findings.lean_check:
import CandleLean.HolSemantics
open HOL Candle.Mlstring Candle.HolSyntax Candle.HolSemantics

theorem instance_outside_spec {U : Type} (i : interpretation U) (name : mlstring) (ty : type) :
    instance_ FEMPTY i name ty = fun _ => tmaof i name [] := by
  have hn : ¬ ∃ ty0 tyin, FLOOKUP (FEMPTY : FMap mlstring type) name = some ty0 ∧ ty = TYPE_SUBST tyin ty0 := by
    intro hex
    obtain ⟨ty0, tyin, h, _⟩ := hex
    simp [FLOOKUP, FEMPTY] at h
  unfold instance_
  exact dif_neg hn
